priced_in_summary: Not TOO_LATE. The method's test asks whether the decomposition shows multiple expansion eating the runway, and here it does not: trailing P/E fell over the past year (roughly 69x to roughly 61x) even as the price rose 46.26%, because FY2025 earnings grew faster than the stock. That rules out the specific TOO_LATE shape even though the stock is expensive in absolute terms (P/E ~61-69x) and sits well above where it traded a year ago. What the price does ask for, on the market's own 2.5-to-1 preferred five-year reverse-DCF convention, is a FCF growth rate (~36%) far beyond anything this dive can defend from the company's own guidance (mid-teens revenue growth) and historical margin range, while the same price is far easier to defend on the ten-year convention (19.75% implied, close to this dive's own 14.41% build). Combined with the chain's own finding that this is the single most crowded link on the map, riding a sector-wide rearmament re-rating rather than a Hormuz-specific one, and a capture link to the actual cited occurrence that is thematic rather than contractual (the CENTCOM operation names a competitor's platform, not Elbit's), the honest verdict is WATCH: a real company on a real growth path, priced for more than this dive can defend at the horizon the market itself prefers.

rows.why: No disagreement, and saying so is worth a row. 2.5% perpetual growth is a reasonable long-run nominal assumption for a diversified global defense-electronics prime with a structural rearmament tailwind, and this dive would not move it. The assumption this dive would question is the discount rate: 9% is not obviously wrong for an Israeli industrial with a net-cash balance sheet, but the file publishes no sensitivity to it beyond the horizon table, and this dive's own 7% stress (see bear[0]) shows the gap survives even a materially friendlier rate. Method section 7 forbids re-solving in session for the filed column itself; the stress computation is disclosed separately as this dive's own sensitivity, not a replacement for the filed number.

rows.note: Built like for like rather than compared revenue-against-FCF. Revenue 7,938,627,000 compounding at 13% for five years gives 14,626,405,660 in FY2030; at a 9.0% steady-state operating margin that is operating income of 1,316,376,509 against 671,424,000 in FY2025; holding FY2025's own cash-conversion ratio (free cash flow over operating income, 552,810,000 / 671,424,000 = 0.8233) gives FY2030 free cash flow of 1,083,824,972, a 14.41% FCF CAGR from the 552,810,000 base. Against the filed 5-year market-implied 35.96%, the gap is 21.55 percentage points, well outside the file's own 16.21-point horizon_spread: a real gap by the file's own rule. Against the filed 10-year market-implied 19.75%, the same 14.41% build is only 5.34 points behind, INSIDE the horizon_spread: not a real gap by the file's own rule. The sign does not flip between horizons (both say the market wants more than this dive defends), only the SIZE of the finding does, and this dive claims the 5-year reading as the operative one because that is the convention the filed solve defaults to and the one the would_buy_zone below is drawn against, consistent with this analyst's prior VRT/HUBB/MYRG dives choosing the tougher convention. Declared and stressed, not just declared: (1) the cash-conversion assumption is the most volatile input in this file's own build (free cash flow over operating income has run 0.0951, -0.1987, 0.6534, 0.8233 across FY2022-FY2025); reverting to the 4-year average (0.3433) instead of holding FY2025's ratio turns the FY2030 FCF outcome to 451,921,581, BELOW today's base, a NEGATIVE 3.95% CAGR, widening rather than closing the gap. This dive defends holding the elevated ratio rather than the volatile average because the growing contract-liabilities balance (+21.95% year over year, bull[1]) is a structural, not incidental, reason to expect the funding pattern behind FY2025's conversion to persist, but the alternate reading is disclosed rather than hidden. (2) The base-FCF sensitivity cuts the same way: using the file's own 3-4 year trailing-average base instead of the elevated FY2025 print does NOT flatter this dive's own build the way it did on MYRG or 688425.SS, because a smaller starting base must grow FASTER, not slower, to reach the same market-implied enterprise value (66.70% at 5y on the 4-year average base, 58.45% on the 3-year average), so choosing the FY2025 base is if anything the more generous reading toward the bull case, not a hidden inflation of the gap. (3) The discount-rate sensitivity (bear[0]) shows the 5-year gap does not close even at a friendlier 7% rate (25.03% implied, still 10.62 points above this dive's 14.41%). (4) [red team, PRICED_IN_CHECK] Forward-solving quality.reverse_dcf's own bisection formula at this dive's own 14.41% build (base_fcf 552,810,000, 9% discount rate, 2.5% terminal growth) instead of solving for g gives a fair price of $321.42 at the 5-year convention (54.16% below the $701.22 reference) and $474.85 at the 10-year convention (32.28% below reference). The 10-year convention narrows the growth-rate gap to 5.34 points but does not remove it in price terms: even the gentler duration still prices this dive's own most defensible build at less than half today's close's remaining distance closed. Choosing the 5-year convention as operative therefore softens the SIZE of the finding rather than manufacturing it: real daylight between price and this dive's own defended fundamentals survives under either horizon, only its magnitude changes.

independence_test.largest_disagreement: The market's 5-year reverse-DCF convention asks for a durable ~36% FCF CAGR (or ~25% even at a materially lower 7% discount rate), while this dive's own like-for-like build, using the company's own 'mid-teens' revenue guidance and a moderate, trend-consistent margin-expansion path, defends roughly 14.41%. The disagreement is horizon-shaped rather than direction-shaped: at the market's own 10-year convention the ask falls to 19.75%, only 5.34 points above this dive's own number and inside the file's 16.21-point horizon spread, so the same price is far easier to defend as a decade-long compounding story than as a five-year one.
independence_test.why_the_gap_exists: The single most crowded link on the entire hormuz-maritime chain (crowdedness 72/100, zero of four repricing-check legs met) is pricing a broad, sector-wide European/US rearmament re-rating that predates and is largely unconnected to the Hormuz occurrence: the 52-week high was set 2026-03-17, a full month before CENTCOM even announced the mine-clearance operation (2026-04-11), and CENTCOM's own cited source names a competitor's platform (General Dynamics' Knifefish), not Elbit's Seagull, for that specific operation. The category of error is a sector-wide re-rating compressed onto a five-year single-issuer DCF window, applied to a name whose own specific tie to the cited occurrence is thematic (same product category) rather than contractual (no cited source attaches a Seagull order, dollar figure, or confirmed role to this mission). pre_mortem.premise: It is 2027-09-04, twelve months after this dive, and the WATCH call was wrong.
reasons: The sector-wide rearmament re-rating proved durable rather than a peak, and Elbit's own fundamentals outran even the market's ambitious ask: operating margin kept climbing past 9.5% (this dive's own independence_test.falsification trigger) rather than slowing to this dive's assumed 9.0%, backlog conversion accelerated beyond the guided 'mid-teens' path, and the 36% five-year FCF-CAGR ask, while extreme against history, was validated by actual results rather than by multiple expansion. This dive's own base case (13% revenue, 9.0% margin) would then have been the conservative read, not the defensible one, and staying at WATCH meant missing a continuation of an already-underway re-rate.

A concrete, disclosed Hormuz or wider-Gulf naval contract converted Elbit's thematic Seagull exposure into a confirmed, dollar-figured role, and given how reactive coverage of this name already is (a beat that still produced an 8.27% one-day decline on valuation grounds), the market re-rated hard on the news alone, faster than the reverse-DCF math could catch up. This dive's own capture skepticism (bear[2]), while factually accurate about the CENTCOM source naming a competitor's platform, turned out to describe a lagging rather than a permanent state.

Risk appetite for high-multiple defense names sustained itself on macro and geopolitical sentiment (continued or escalating Gulf tensions, rising global defense budgets) independent of whether ESLT's own fundamentals closed the gap this dive measured, and no company-specific catalyst forced a reversion inside the 90-day COMPOUNDER clock; the trailing P/E, already falling even as price rose, simply kept falling as earnings kept outrunning an already-expensive price, without the multiple-expansion shape method section 7 would need to call this TOO_LATE in hindsight either.
pre_mortem.why_the_market_could_have_been_right: Reason 1 is the most concrete and checkable: this dive's own operating_margin row already documents a genuine, filing-verified multi-year trend (6.18% to 7.16% to 8.46%, FY2023-2025, roughly 100-130bp of expansion in each of the last two years) and deliberately assumes that pace slows to roughly half rather than continuing. If it does not slow, the file's own falsification condition (margin at or above 9.5%) fires exactly as designed, and the structural case for further margin expansion (record backlog, a growing customer-advance base funding working capital ahead of revenue recognition) is already named in this file as the reason the market might be right, not manufactured for this pre-mortem.
pre_mortem.downgrade_note: The verdict is already at WATCH, the floor an unanswerable pre-mortem would impose, and a coherent, filing-grounded market-would-have-been-right story is namable and ties directly to this file's own falsification condition, so the pre-mortem informs the file without forcing further change, the same non-effect this analyst's log recorded for HUBB and MYRG.

would_buy_zone.basis: The band at which this dive's own net_gap_direction like-for-like build would close the gap against the filed 5-year reverse-DCF convention (35.96% headline), the tougher of the two horizons the file solves (vs 19.75% at 10 years) and the convention this dive claims as operative. Low = $282.94 is the price at which that convention's implied ask falls to a conservative build (11% revenue CAGR, 8.5% steady-state margin, FY2025 cash conversion held, FCF CAGR 11.11%). High = $364.23 is the price at which it falls to a stretch build (15% revenue CAGR, 9.5% margin, same conversion, FCF CAGR 17.70%), above this dive's own 13%/9.0%/14.41% base case. Both solved by forward-evaluating quality.reverse_dcf's own bisection formula (base_fcf $552,810,000, 9% discount rate, 2.5% terminal growth, 5-year horizon; this dive's replication reproduces the filed 5/7/10-year readings exactly before varying the target) at a chosen g instead of solving for g, then converting enterprise value to price via the file's own net-cash bridge (net cash $617,141,000, 46,442,352 FY2025 shares: price = (EV + net cash) / shares). [red team, ENTRY_BASIS_STRESS] The zone sits 48.06%-59.65% below the $701.22 reference, the deepest zone-to-spot gap this analyst has drawn (VRT -40.4/-44.9%, HUBB -17.6/-33.6%, MYRG -53.6/-61.5%), so this dive checked whether the depth is a convention artifact rather than a real level: forward-solving the same formula at this dive's own 14.41% base case gives a fair price of $321.42 at the 5-year convention used here (between the zone's own low and high, as it should be) and $474.85 at the 10-year convention, 32.28% below the $701.22 reference. The 10-year anchor is deliberately excluded as the zone's basis for the same reason VRT's red team excluded its own 10-year point: accepting the market's own preferred, gentler duration would make the zone spot with a haircut rather than a real margin of safety, exactly the question the independence test leaves open. That the gentler anchor still sits nearly a third below spot is why this zone's depth is treated as real daylight rather than a formality.
